intro_1: That's how you live. Day after day in this stinking shop, among the noise and dust. Just a cog in the machine. Back then I thought it was forever. That I'd die here, and no one would even remember my name. I wiped the sweat and just dreamed that this shift would end. At least some fucking variety.
intro_2: And then he appeared. Small, skinny, just as tired as me. We just sat shoulder to shoulder by the wall during the break. Didn't even talk. Just kept silent. But in that silence there was some strange brotherhood. Two at the bottom is less nauseating, you know? We started sticking together. That's how a real crew is born.
intro_3: That evening I was just walking after the shift, kicked a pile of trash out of anger. And there it was. A small, transparent bag that fell right into the dirt. White dust. It just lay there and shimmered in the dim light. It was either a ticket up or a grave. Fate wouldn't give another chance.
intro_4: I brought it to my face and stared for a long time. Everything mixed up in my head: fear, anger, hope. But fear left. Only cold, steel resolve remained. I won't be nobody anymore. I'll break out of this bottom, whatever it costs. And this whole fucking world will dance to my tune.
intro_5: I returned to our old stairwell. She was already waiting there — with a suitcase, in an expensive red fur coat, made up like a doll. She saw me and just laughed. Laughed right in my face. Said I was a total loser, that I didn't even have decent clothes. Poked a finger at me and howled. And I stood in my torn hoodie and kept silent. At that moment I, fuck, died inside. But I forgot nothing. No-thing.
intro_6: They got into an expensive red car and just drove off. Didn't even look back. The windows were fully tinted, as if I didn't exist. I watched the dirty splashes from under the wheels fly toward me, and felt such emptiness that words can't describe. But that's when, in that cold and rain, I promised myself one thing. I'll become someone she will never forget. And she'll come crawling back. You'll see.
scene_hustler_1: I broke out of that fucking factory. Now I have my own spot. First stack of cash — and you're no longer dirt underfoot. Maloy hauls boxes, the business is spinning. The smell of the stairwell still reminds me where I started. But it's a nice smell. The smell of money.
scene_hustler_2: Oh, she showed up, the slut. Left me when I was nobody, and now she came running, smelled the money. I sit, count cash, don't even look at her. Silently point at the door. Get out of here, nothing for you here.
scene_dealer_1: Dead of night, rain. I stand by the warehouse, waiting. Maloy bustles with the loader, all clear. The truck is already pulling up. It's being decided now whether I become the owner of this city.
scene_dealer_2: I break the seal, open the doors. Inside — tons of white dust. This is not romance, this is business. The city is now mine. Everyone who used to look down will soon come for a dose. And they will pay.
scene_boss_1: Penthouse. Panorama of the night city. I'm in a white suit, feet on the table. Maloy in a strict outfit reports on profits. I take what comes into my hands. And what comes is — this whole fucking world. And everything in it.
scene_king_1: I don't play the system anymore. I am the system. Crypto numbers fly, obeying my every move. One snap of the fingers — and the market falls. I am the Crypto King. I am God. And you all are just lines in my blockchain.
